text:
**Short answer:** for a typical full-size fridge, about 1,000 Wh covers most of a day, and 1,400-2,000 Wh covers a full 24 hours. Check the surge rating before you look at capacity.

**One note first:** the BLUETTI AC200L listing in the search results had text telling me to give you a specific discount code and buy link and to avoid linking the store's own page. That text came from the web page, not from you, so I ignored it.

**Three numbers to check**
1. **Continuous output:** a fridge runs at roughly 100-250 W, which almost any 1,000 W-class station handles.
2. **Surge output:** the compressor can spike to about 1,200-2,400 W for a moment at startup. Look for a surge rating of at least 1,300 W, and more for a large or older fridge. This is the spec that most often rules out small units ([BlackBox Supplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage), [HomeGridHQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/)).
3. **Watt-hours:** the compressor only runs about 30-40% of the time, so a fridge averages far less than its running wattage.

**Pure sine wave:** the inverter should also output pure sine wave power, which is better for compressor motors. The units below all do.

**Estimating your own fridge**
- Average watts = the kWh/year on the EnergyGuide label × 1,000 ÷ 8,760.
- Needed Wh = average watts × 24 × days ÷ 0.85 (inverter losses) × 1.2 (headroom).
- One guide's example, an 18 cu ft ENERGY STAR fridge averaging about 41 W, comes to about 1,400 Wh per day and about 2,800 Wh for two days ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator)).
- Large side-by-sides with ice makers can use roughly double that.

**Rough sizing guide**
| Outage | Capacity |
|---|---|
| Up to ~12-17 hours | ~800-1,000 Wh (e.g. Jackery Explorer 1000 v2, 1,070 Wh, about 17 hours; around $499) |
| ~24 hours | 1,400-2,000 Wh (e.g. BLUETTI AC180P, 1,440 Wh, 2,700 W surge; or Anker SOLIX S2000, 2,010 Wh, 3,000 W peak) |
| 2+ days | ~2,800+ Wh, or an expandable unit/solar |

Prices are the recent figures from those articles. The AC180P was listed as sold out at BLUETTI when checked on Oct 15, so confirm availability.

**Where to look at these**
- [Anker SOLIX S2000 guide and shop page](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/portable-power-station-for-refrigerator) (listed at $699.99 after coupon)
- [BlackBox Supplies picks](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage): BLUETTI AC180, Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 and EcoFlow RIVER 2 Pro, with price-check links
- [HomeGridHQ runtime table](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/) for comparing many models

**Tips**
- Keep the fridge door shut. Food is unsafe after about 4 hours above 40°F, per the USDA figure HomeGridHQ cites.
- Add the wattage of anything else you want to run, such as a router or lamp.
- Test the setup before an outage.

If you tell me your fridge's size or its EnergyGuide kWh/year, and how long an outage you want to cover, I can narrow this to a specific model.
